target.title: RFC 0016: Command Catalog
target.body:
## What this RFC proposes

A read-only **Command Catalog** built from command information OpenClaw already owns. It compares two concrete public shapes without changing command execution, permissions, or policy.

### Option A: broader catalog

```text
openclaw catalog list
openclaw catalog audit
openclaw catalog test-matrix
openclaw catalog summary
```

This option joins CLI descriptors, routes, runtime/plugin commands, and selected command-like tool adapters, then adds operational lenses.

- [Upstream draft](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100960)
- [Foundation](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/11)
- [Dynamic/operator lenses](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/12)

### Option B: narrower commands surface

```text
openclaw commands list
openclaw commands inspect <command-path...>
```

This option follows noun-based groups such as `plugins` and `skills`, stays command-owned, and excludes the aggregate audit/test/summary reports and ownerless tool adapters.

- [Commands list](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/24)
- [Commands inspect](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/25)

OpenClaw already has a Gateway `commands.list` RPC for agent-facing chat/native/skill/plugin commands. Neither option replaces that RPC; the RFC calls out the naming overlap and leaves future convergence explicit.

## Shared boundary

Both options are read-only views over existing registries. They do not dispatch commands or enforce policy. The proposed source metadata remains small: effect mode, optional risk/confirmation, and public/internal exposure where the owning registry knows those facts.

## Feedback requested

- Is the broader `catalog` boundary useful, or is `commands` cleaner and more familiar?
- Should command-like tools remain outside the initial command inventory?
- How should either option eventually relate to Gateway `commands.list` and live paired-node command declarations?
- Which JSON fields should be stable beyond schema version, identity, and provenance?

target.title: RFC: Claws
target.body:
## Summary

- Defines one Claw package as one complete new OpenClaw agent for one job.
- Makes `claws add` create a new `agents.list[]` entry and workspace; existing agent/workspace collisions fail closed.
- Uses grouped `agent`, `workspace`, `packages`, `mcpServers`, and `cronJobs` ownership boundaries.
- Keeps skills, plugins, MCP servers, heartbeat, and Gateway cron on their existing OpenClaw owner surfaces.
- Uses enclosing `package.json` plus authenticated publishing for package identity, version, and publisher ownership.
- Excludes models, providers, credentials, channel bindings, `agent.skills`, and generic connectors from the portable contract.
- Gates the draft CLI behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`; when disabled, the command is unregistered and absent from help and completions.

## Lifecycle and safety

The lifecycle is `add`, `status`, `update`, `remove`, and `export`. Read-only plans precede consented mutation. Unsupported, blocked, drifted, or ambiguous ownership fails closed.

Grouped update rebuilds its plan immediately before mutation, uses each owner's strongest compare-and-swap or convergence boundary, advances root provenance last, and compensates completed owners in reverse order. Uncertain config/Gateway calls and package installs without artifact rollback are reported as partial rather than cross-owner atomic.

## Control UI alignment

[openclaw/openclaw#103176](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103176) remains the Control UI surface for plugin inventory, installation, enablement/disablement, removal, and curated MCP connector discovery. Claws add package references to the shared lifecycle model; removing a Claw releases its reference and does not silently uninstall a shared plugin or skill. A global plugin pinned to another version by a different Claw fails update closed.

Portable MCP declarations remain direct validated `mcp.servers` configuration and do not create a feed-backed connector identity or replace the Control UI's curated connector shelf.

## Implementation stack

The RFC now links the ordered eleven-PR OpenClaw stack:

1. [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) grouped schema and add planning
2. [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) agent/root install
3. [#101973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) managed workspace files
4. [#102228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) ClawHub packages and shared uninstall warnings
5. [#102296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102296) status/remove
6. [#102306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102306) export
7. [#102383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102383) Gateway cron ownership
8. [#102406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102406) stdio/remote MCP ownership
9. [#102427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102427) lifecycle diagnostics
10. [#102959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959) grouped update planning
11. [#102982](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102982) consented grouped update apply

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- line-wrapping and rendered Markdown structure scan
- all linked PR heads, bases, titles, and open state verified live
- consistency review against Patrick Erichsen's product/schema boundaries and merged Control UI PR #103176
